messages:
devon: Heads up — seeing spike in outbound errors from inference sidecars in us-west-2. NATs are hitting port limits per EIP, lots of connection resets to model-fetch endpoints, ~20% 502s on model startup pulls. Anyone oncall?
ashley: Confirmed in Datadog dashboards — SYN rates and TIME_WAIT counts skyrocketing on nodes serving sidecars. Affected nodes are opening thousands of short-lived outbound TCP connections to object storage and the model registry.
sam: Is this tied to the recent change that shards pull models independently? We removed some shared caching this week.
maria: Yep — sidecars currently open a new TCP for each shard pull with no keepalive reuse. I can push a small change to enable HTTP/2 + connection pooling.
kai: Short-term mitigation: add additional EIPs to the NAT gateway and spin up a standby NAT in another AZ. Also consider routing heavy model-fetch traffic through a small fleet of egress proxies that multiplex connections.
devon: I'm spinning up an egress-proxy ASG now and queuing a quick k8s node sysctl patch to widen ip_local_port_range and enable tcp_tw_reuse. Reminder: widening helps but is still bounded per-source IP. Any objections to the node-level sysctl?
ashley: Widening the range helps headroom but doesn't solve per-EIP port ceiling. App-level reduction in churn is the safer approach. Kernel tweaks on all nodes could have side effects; prefer canary first.
sam: deploy-bot: starting canary of sidecar with connection pooling on 3 pods in us-west-2a. Will watch for ephemeral port usage.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: inference-sidecar v1.8.3 -> 3 pods (us-west-2a). Logs: /services/inference/sidecar — follow for rollout status.
maria: Pushed patch enabling HTTP2 multiplexing and keepalive reuse. Example config snippet: `ENABLE_HTTP2=true; HTTP2_MAX_STREAMS=100; KEEPALIVE=60s` — also added a small exponential backoff on model pull retries.
kai: Added a soft concurrency throttle for model pulls per pod (was 8 -> now 2) in the sidecar config to smooth bursts.
ashley: Creating Grafana alert: if ephemeral port usage per EIP > 58k for >2m, trigger route-shift to standby NAT and page infra. Also adding metric for TIME_WAIT/sec.
devon: Canary looks good after 12m: 502 rate down from 20% -> 1.5%, TIME_WAIT count down ~60%. Keeping canary for 30m before rolling. Plan: provision an extra NAT gateway in us-west-2b for redundancy and add egress-proxy as a persistent layer.
sam: Long term ticket created INF-4881: build global egress proxy with SNI reuse, connection multiplexing, and per-customer connection pools to reduce source port fanout and lower NAT dependence.
maria: Updated runbook with mitigation steps (rotate EIPs, scale egress proxies, enable sidecar HTTP/2, sysctl as last resort). cc @kai @ashley :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Automated remediation note: when alert fires, run `kubectl scale deploy/egress-proxy --replicas=4 -n infra` then `ip route replace` is on runbook.
devon: Follow-up actions: roll v1.8.3 to us-west-2 with the pooling flag, provision natgw-usw2b, and schedule post-mortem to capture root cause and preventive quotas on model pull concurrency. Thanks all for fast turnaround.
